growth_stages.name: Nursery
growth_stages.description: Seedlings raised for 35-45 days before transplanting. Day 0 is transplanting, not seed sowing -- same convention as tomato.json/pepper.json.

operations.name: Seed/Variety Selection
operations.description: Choice of long-storage red types (Sokoto/Kano red local, improved Red Creole/Bombay Red) suited to the aggregation and trade market.

operations.name: Land Preparation
operations.description: Preparing fine, well-drained beds -- onions specifically dislike waterlogging. The source ruleset does not separately name a land-clearing step for this crop, same pattern as yam.json; kept as a single operation to stay faithful to the source rather than imposing an unstated split.

operations.name: Transplanting
operations.description: Transplanting seedlings at ~10-15cm x 10cm spacing for good bulb size and packing density. This is day 0 of the field lifecycle.

operations.name: Nitrogen Application
operations.description: Early nitrogen application only -- late nitrogen causes 'thick necks' that fail to seal and rot in store.

operations.name: Irrigation
operations.description: Consistent irrigation through the growing season, stopped before harvest to aid field curing. The 'stop before harvest' half of this guidance is an absence/cessation-based instruction (do X, then STOP doing X) that this schema's validation_rules cannot represent -- rules only fire when an operation IS logged, not when one continues past a point it should have ended. Same category of limitation as tomato_r4b's staking reminder in tomato.json. No validation_rule is attached to this operation for that reason.

operations.name: Curing (Field Curing)
operations.description: Field-curing with tops attached for 7-14 days before storage -- the primary rot-prevention step for this crop, and what enables the long shelf-life this crop is grown for.

validation_rules.condition: PLATFORM BUGFIX: this dependency rule did not exist at all in the original file, meaning transplanting could previously be logged with NO land_preparation in history whatsoever (not even same-day -- any day, or never). Added in response to a real bug the user found: land preparation needs to happen and be given at least a day before the next stage begins, not be skippable or same-day. min=1 day (not 0) so same-day submissions are also blocked, consistent with the same fix applied to every other crop file in this pass.
validation_rules.source: N/A -- internal platform bugfix, not new agronomic sourcing. Max-day window (21 days) matches the convention used for equivalent rules in this knowledge base's other annual/nursery-transplant crops.

validation_rules.condition: Hard block if the nursery is under 20 or over 60 days.
validation_rules.source: AgTrail Master Agronomist & Validator Ruleset, Agrolinking Solutions Ltd., July 2026, Section 14 (Onion), Stage 1.

validation_rules.condition: Flag under 30 or over 50 days -- over-aged seedlings bulb prematurely in the bed. Sits inside the 20-60 day hard-block window.
validation_rules.source: AgTrail Master Agronomist & Validator Ruleset, Agrolinking Solutions Ltd., July 2026, Section 14 (Onion), Stage 1.

validation_rules.condition: Hard block if nitrogen is logged after 60 DAT. No floor: the source states 'apply N early only' without a stated minimum-days threshold, so none is invented here.
validation_rules.source: AgTrail Master Agronomist & Validator Ruleset, Agrolinking Solutions Ltd., July 2026, Section 14 (Onion), Stage 3.

validation_rules.condition: Flag after 45 DAT -- late nitrogen causes 'thick necks' that fail to seal and rot in store.
validation_rules.source: AgTrail Master Agronomist & Validator Ruleset, Agrolinking Solutions Ltd., July 2026, Section 14 (Onion), Stage 3.

validation_rules.condition: Hard block before 75 DAT -- early bulbs are watery and unmarketable. No upper block: the source states no ceiling for this crop's harvest timing, same pattern as yam.json and groundnut.json.
validation_rules.source: AgTrail Master Agronomist & Validator Ruleset, Agrolinking Solutions Ltd., July 2026, Section 14 (Onion), Stage 4.

validation_rules.condition: Flag before 85 DAT. Sits above the 75-day hard-block floor: harvest logged between 75 and 85 days is physically accepted but flagged, since the stated typical window starts at 90 DAT.
validation_rules.source: AgTrail Master Agronomist & Validator Ruleset, Agrolinking Solutions Ltd., July 2026, Section 14 (Onion), Stage 4.

validation_rules.condition: Harvest can only be logged once per planting cycle for this template -- unlike tomato/pepper, onion is a single bulb-lift crop, not a repeated-picking crop.
validation_rules.source: Inherited convention from this knowledge base's other single-harvest crop files -- not separately addressed in the source ruleset for this crop.

validation_rules.condition: Hard block if logged to warehouse storage without a curing record existing first. Same mechanic as groundnut_r_storage_requires_drying in groundnut.json: engine.validator already produces a hard block whenever a rule's declared dependency has no matching entry in history, regardless of the severity set here.
validation_rules.source: AgTrail Master Agronomist & Validator Ruleset, Agrolinking Solutions Ltd., July 2026, Section 14 (Onion), Stage 4.

validation_rules.condition: MODELING ASSUMPTION, same as groundnut_r_drying_duration_warn in groundnut.json: the source says 'flag if curing is under 5 days -- uncured onions rot in store,' describing a DURATION this schema's single-date operations cannot represent directly. Approximated by treating the curing operation's logged date as when field-curing began, and requiring storage to be logged at least 5 days after that as a proxy for 'curing lasted at least 5 days.' Note the source's own typical curing duration is stated as 7-14 days -- this rule only checks the stated 5-day minimum, not the 14-day typical upper bound, since no warning is stated in the source for curing longer than typical.
validation_rules.source: AgTrail Master Agronomist & Validator Ruleset, Agrolinking Solutions Ltd., July 2026, Section 14 (Onion), Stage 4.

validation_rules.condition: Global rule: no operation may be logged with a date earlier than the previous operation's logged date for the same farm/cycle (no backdating that would reorder the sequence).
validation_rules.source: Inherited convention across this knowledge base.

validation_rules.condition: PLATFORM BUGFIX (second sweep): this dependency rule did not exist at all in the original file -- land_preparation could previously be logged with no nursery_establishment in its history whatsoever. Found via a systematic audit of every consecutive REQUIRED-to-REQUIRED workflow step pair across all 20 crops, run after the user asked whether the land-prep sequencing fix generalized to every stage. It did not, until this pass. min=1 day so same-day submissions are also caught, consistent with every other sequencing fix in this knowledge base.
validation_rules.source: N/A -- internal platform bugfix, not new agronomic sourcing. Max-day window (60 days) is a reasonable platform default matching similar transitions elsewhere in this file, not independently sourced from the Master Ruleset for this specific pair.

validation_rules.condition: PLATFORM BUGFIX (second sweep): this dependency rule did not exist at all in the original file -- curing could previously be logged with no harvest in its history whatsoever. Found via a systematic audit of every consecutive REQUIRED-to-REQUIRED workflow step pair across all 20 crops, run after the user asked whether the land-prep sequencing fix generalized to every stage. It did not, until this pass. min=1 day so same-day submissions are also caught, consistent with every other sequencing fix in this knowledge base.
validation_rules.source: N/A -- internal platform bugfix, not new agronomic sourcing. Max-day window (5 days) is a reasonable platform default matching similar transitions elsewhere in this file, not independently sourced from the Master Ruleset for this specific pair.

soil_requirements.drainage: well-drained -- onions specifically dislike waterlogging, per the source ruleset's Stage 1 guidance

weather_preferences.notes: Not covered numerically in the source ruleset section for this crop beyond the qualitative waterlogging note (reflected in soil_requirements.drainage above). CORRECTED: an initial draft of this field left these as null, since this is predominantly described as a dry-season IRRIGATED crop in the source ruleset's own framing and rainfall figures could be misleading for a crop whose water is normally supplied by irrigation, not rain -- but the schema requires integer/number types here, not null, so null would have failed schema validation. These figures are placeholder rainfall-equivalent/temperature ranges carried over from general West African dry-season onion agronomy references, same caveat as yam.json's and groundnut.json's weather_preferences placeholders. Flagged for agronomist review, and flagged as a genuine schema constraint worth knowing about: this crop file structurally cannot express 'not applicable, this crop uses irrigation, not rainfall' -- only a numeric placeholder.

pests.name: Thrips
pests.symptoms: Silvery leaf streaking/scarring from rasping-sucking feeding, reduced bulb size under heavy pressure.
pests.management: Scouting and vector control per the source ruleset's IPM guidance; consistent irrigation also reduces thrips pressure, which favors hot, dry conditions.
pests.source: AgTrail Master Agronomist & Validator Ruleset, Agrolinking Solutions Ltd., July 2026, Section 14 (Onion), Stage 3 ('Manage thrips; irrigate consistently...').

yield_model.notes: Range taken directly from the source ruleset's stated Pass tier, extended slightly at the top to close a gap in its stated tiers -- see yield_validation source note.

tiers.message: Must be logged as a Disaster/Loss Event, not a harvest record.
Poor yield -- thrips or weed pressure.
Exceptional; verify improved genetics and drip irrigation.
Biological maximum exceeded for West African conditions.

yield_validation.source: AgTrail Master Agronomist & Validator Ruleset, Agrolinking Solutions Ltd., July 2026, Section 14 (Onion), Yield Validation table. Two things resolved rather than transcribed as-is: (1) the table's own text states Pass as '5.0-25.0 t/ha' and Soft Warning as '>35.0 t/ha', leaving 25.0-35.0 covered by neither -- same gap pattern as yam.json/groundnut.json/pepper.json, resolved the same way, by extending Pass to 5.0-35.0. (2) UNLIKE groundnut.json and maize's source table, this crop's table has no explicit '0 t/ha' row and its prefacing note reads differently ('practical floor is the low soft-warning band' -- a comment about realistic reporting range, not an explicit 'zero = loss event' instruction like groundnut's). An equals_zero tier is still added here for consistency with the rest of this knowledge base and because yield_validator.py requires every possible value to match some tier or it raises an error -- but flagged explicitly that, unlike other crops, this specific tier is NOT directly stated in this crop's source section and should be confirmed against ruleset-author intent.

version_history.changed_by: AgTrail Knowledge Base - new crop, Medium-priority tier, built from Master Ruleset
version_history.summary: Initial file for Onion (Allium cepa), fourth of the 8 Medium-priority crops from the AgTrail Master Agronomist & Validator Ruleset not yet in this knowledge base, built from Section 14. Unlike pepper.json, this crop's source section gives fully explicit hard-block/soft-warning number pairs for nearly every rule, which also happen to fit this engine's existing 'outside a window' rule mechanic cleanly (a single rule with both min and max correctly represents 'block under 20 or over 60 days' in one rule, no interior-band problem the way groundnut.json's weeding rule had). Two items still required explicit flagging rather than direct transcription: (1) the curing-duration rule ('flag if curing is under 5 days') is the same DURATION-as-single-date-proxy limitation already flagged in groundnut.json's drying rule -- modeled the same way, with the same caveat about depending on curing being logged at its start. (2) The yield_validation table has the same 25.0-35.0 t/ha gap pattern as yam.json/groundnut.json/pepper.json, resolved the same way, PLUS a genuinely different wrinkle: unlike those crops, this crop's source table has no explicit '0 t/ha' row and its prefacing note doesn't use the explicit 'zero = loss event' language groundnut.json's did -- the equals_zero tier is added anyway for schema-safety and knowledge-base consistency, but flagged as not directly stated for this specific crop, unlike every other crop file's equals_zero tier so far. Also left weather_preferences numerically empty rather than guessed, since the source explicitly frames this as a dry-season IRRIGATED crop -- rainfall figures would misrepresent how the crop is actually watered. The irrigation operation's 'stop before harvest' guidance was also flagged as an absence/cessation-based instruction this schema's validation_rules architecture cannot represent, the same category of gap as tomato.json's staking-reminder note. Not yet agronomist-reviewed.
version_history.source: AgTrail Master Agronomist & Validator Ruleset, Agrolinking Solutions Ltd., July 2026, Section 14 (Onion).

version_history.changed_by: AgTrail Knowledge Base - platform bugfix, land-prep sequencing gate
version_history.summary: Added onion_r_land_prep_gate, a dependency rule that was MISSING ENTIRELY from this file, in response to a real bug the user found while using the platform: the affected operation(s) could previously be logged with no preceding dependency in history at all -- not same-day, not any particular window, just completely unenforced. Confirmed via a test submission with empty history before this fix (the operation passed clean with zero warnings). Now requires at least 1 day after the dependency, closing the gap. This is a data-authoring fix (a rule that should have existed but didn't), not an engine bug.

version_history.summary: Added onion_r_seq_nursery_establishment_land_preparation, onion_r_seq_harvest_curing. Found via a systematic audit of every consecutive REQUIRED-to-REQUIRED workflow step pair across all 20 crops, run after the user asked whether the land-prep sequencing fix (first sweep) generalized to every stage transition. It did not -- this file had one or more later-stage transitions where the next required step could be logged with no record of the preceding required step ever existing, the same bug class as the original land-prep gap. min=1 day so same-day submissions are also caught. Confirmed via scenario testing that the affected operation(s) now correctly require their dependency to exist first.
